A0245.title: Financial Reconciliation
A0245.definition: Collect order, payment, refund, fulfillment, and settlement records to reconcile amount, status, and fund-flow consistency by transaction.
A0245.description:
Financial reconciliation collects order payable amounts, processor-paid amounts, refund amounts, fees, discount subsidies, fulfillment states, settlement batches, and channel statements, then reconciles them by order number, payment order number, processor transaction ID, and settlement date. The system can use rules, thresholds, and difference lists to identify mismatched order and payment amounts, refunds that did not roll back discounts, duplicate settlement, missing settlement, or abnormal low-price transactions.

This control detects fund differences caused by payment amount tampering, low-price purchase, discount stacking arbitrage, and payment callback anomalies, and provides evidence for transaction closure and recovery. Implementation should automatically route abnormal differences to fulfillment freezing, manual review, channel inquiry, and recovery workflows instead of only producing reports.
A0245.limitation: Financial reconciliation often has end-of-day or batch delays, so attackers may complete fulfillment, withdrawal, or resale before differences are found. Inconsistent field definitions across orders, payments, refunds, and channel statements can also create false positives or missed findings. Reconciliation detects differences after they occur, so it still needs server-side recalculation, payment inquiry, and idempotency controls to reduce pre-event bypasses.
